entries.proposition: DESIGN: ovalbumin-sensitised male Brown Norway rats, 10 weeks, anaesthetised and ventilated; six groups across two steps with n of 10 (7 in the shock group of step one); epinephrine titrated to a target blood pressure; mitochondrial respiration on left-ventricle fibres at 15 or 60 minutes; lactate by a bedside meter; cardiac output estimated from echocardiographic diameters.
entries.snippet: Ten-week-old male Brown Norway rats (Charles River laboratories, Saint-Germain-Nuelles, France) weighing 250–300 g were sensitized

entries.proposition: The epinephrine regimen is large: two 2.5 microgram boluses then an infusion started at 10 micrograms per kg per minute and titrated every five minutes to a mean arterial pressure of 100 mmHg; the cumulative dose was about 880 micrograms per kg in both treated groups.
entries.snippet: Then, a continuous infusion of epinephrine (10 μg/kg/min) was started at T5 as described previously [4].

entries.proposition: Epinephrine restored pressure and survival to 60 minutes but cardiac mitochondrial respiration stayed impaired: complexes I plus II minus 29 percent and complex II minus 40 percent against control at 60 minutes.
entries.snippet: OXPHOS was significantly impaired in the AS+EPI groups as compared to the control group through complexes I+II (−29%, p < 0.05) and II (−40%, p < 0.001) at T60 min

entries.proposition: ATTRIBUTION: the Discussion says epinephrine might itself provoke cardiomyocyte dysfunction including impaired respiration; the design cannot test it, because the shock-only group was sampled at 15 minutes (it died) and there is no epinephrine-in-non-shocked group; at 15 minutes shock alone already lowered complex II respiration by 36 percent.
entries.snippet: Epinephrine might even provoke cardiomyocyte dysfunction, including impaired mitochondrial respiration, which might participate in the epinephrine refractory cases of AS.
entries.anchor: 3 Discussion, (1) Characterization of AS and effects of epinephrine alone

entries.proposition: LACTATE: at 60 minutes arterial lactate was 4.8 mmol/L in the epinephrine-treated shock group against control and 3.6 with the adjuvant; no shock-only value at a matched time and no epinephrine-only value exist, and the article does not discuss epinephrine-driven glycolysis as a source of lactate.
entries.snippet: arterial lactatemia (Figure 7) was significantly higher in the AS+EPI and AS+EPI+preNBut groups as compared to the CON group (p < 0.0001)

entries.proposition: The contractility readout is the shortening fraction; it rises above control in the epinephrine groups and reaches 100 percent, while cardiac output stays far below control (15 against 62 mL/min), which the figures show is a collapsed end-systolic cavity, not an index of intrinsic contractility.
entries.snippet: In the AS+EPI+preNBut group, LVSF did not decrease and remained at a high level throughout the experiment.

entries.proposition: The cardiac output is a derived estimate (Teichholz from echocardiographic diameters), and the authors state they did not use invasive methods; the formula was validated in clinical echocardiography, not in a rat with a collapsed ventricle.
entries.snippet: First, we did not investigate cardiac output or cardiac contractility with invasive methods

entries.proposition: TRANSLATION: the authors say there is insufficient evidence to justify clinical trials of the adjuvant; the only effective treatment remains epinephrine; the adjuvant was given one hour before the shock, which limits use to predictable risk.
entries.snippet: Concerning the translational potential of the findings, there is insufficient evidence to justify testing NbutGT in clinical trials.

entries.proposition: The statistics paragraph concedes that multiple comparisons raise type I error and that results should be interpreted as containing some biases; group sizes are justified from earlier work in the same model.
entries.snippet: Because of the potential for type I error due to multiple comparisons, results should be interpreted as containing some biases.

entries.proposition: Figure 7: lactate at 60 minutes about 0.9 (control), 4.8 (shock plus epinephrine) and 3.6 mmol/L (plus adjuvant); no shock-only bar exists.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 7 bar chart of arterial lactatemia in mmol/L: CON about 0.9, AS+EPI about 4.8 with four asterisks against CON, AS+EPI+preNBut about 3.6 with one asterisk against AS+EPI.
